title: Devil's Hand: Data Poisoning Attacks to Locally Private Graph Learning Protocols

problem.claim: Locally private graph learning protocols may be vulnerable to data poisoning attacks that compromise the utility of privacy-preserving graph learning.

gap.claim: Previous research had not considered data poisoning attacks against locally private graph learning protocols.

contributions.claim: Introduces a data poisoning attack targeting locally private graph learning protocols by injecting fake users, linking them with genuine users, and sending crafted data to the server.
Explores several defense strategies against the proposed attack.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The effectiveness of the attack is demonstrated theoretically and empirically.
The explored defense strategies have limited effectiveness.

narrative_sequence.summary: GNNs are successful for graph representation learning, but real-world graphs may contain sensitive personal information.
Locally private graph learning protocols combine local differential privacy with GNN message passing to seek privacy and utility.
These protocols may be vulnerable to data poisoning attacks, an issue not considered in previous research.
The work introduces an attack that injects fake users, establishes links with genuine users, and sends crafted data to the server.
The attack is reported as theoretically and empirically effective, while explored defenses show limited effectiveness.

source_observation.claim: A privacy-preserving protocol can remain exposed to poisoning through attacker-controlled participants and links.

interpretation.claim: Privacy protection and poisoning robustness address different threat dimensions.

application.claim: Evaluate privacy-preserving graph learning protocols against adversarial participant injection and link manipulation.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this attack generalizes beyond the described protocol setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the attack algorithm, threat-model assumptions, datasets, metrics, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not identify the explored defense strategies or explain their limitations.
